theme: A no-tomato October: pork & porcini ragu bianco and an olive-oil bean conserva, built for pasta, polenta, seared fish and soup. Just you and Mike this week (girls with Jen).

components.name: Pork & Porcini Ragu Bianco (white ragu)
components.ingredients: 1 lb ground pork, 3 oz pancetta (diced), 1 oz dried porcini, 1 onion + 1 carrot + 1 celery rib (fine soffritto), 2 cloves garlic, 1 cup dry white wine, 1 cup whole milk, parmesan rind, sage/rosemary/bay, olive oil
components.method: Soak porcini in hot water 20 min; save the liquor. Sweat the fine soffritto low and slow in a generous slick of olive oil, 12-15 min, no color. Add pancetta, render, then the pork and brown it hard, breaking it fine. Stir in chopped porcini, pour in the white wine and let it cook off almost completely (sfumatura). Add milk, strained porcini liquor, parmesan rind and herbs; bare simmer uncovered 60-75 min until glossy and unctuous. This is a double batch on purpose: feeds the pappardelle and the polenta dinners, freezes well.

components.name: Olive-Oil Braised Cannellini Conserva
components.ingredients: 1 lb dried cannellini (soaked overnight), 1 head garlic halved, sage + rosemary sprigs, 1 dried chile, 2 bay leaves, ~1/2 cup olive oil, salt (late)
components.method: Drain the soaked beans into a Dutch oven, cover with water by 2 inches, add the halved garlic head, herbs, chile, bay and a big glug of oil. Bring to the barest simmer and cook gently 60-90 min until creamy but intact; salt only in the last 20 min. Cool and store the beans in their own brothy liquor with a film of oil on top. That bean broth is liquid gold for the fish and the ribollita.

dinners.name: Pappardelle al Ragu Bianco
dinners.ingredients: pappardelle, the ragu bianco, butter, parmesan, parsley, pasta water
steps: Boil the pappardelle in well-salted water; reserve a mugful of water.
Loosen a few ladles of ragu in a wide pan with a splash of pasta water.
Pull the pasta a minute early and finish it in the ragu for 60-90 sec.
Off the heat, add cold butter and a handful of parmesan and toss hard with more pasta water until the sauce turns glossy and clings (mantecatura).
Plate, shower with parm and parsley.

dinners.name: Seared Cod over Brothy Cannellini
dinners.ingredients: 2 cod or halibut fillets, the cannellini conserva + liquor, a bunch of kale or escarole, lemon, olive oil
steps: Warm the beans with a ladle of their liquor and the torn greens until the greens wilt; keep it brothy.
Pat the fish bone-dry and season well.
Sear presentation-side down in hot olive oil, spooning the oil over, 3-4 min until golden; flip for just a minute.
Spoon beans and broth into bowls, rest the fish on top.
Finish with a squeeze of lemon and a raw thread of good olive oil.

dinners.name: Soft Polenta with Ragu Bianco
dinners.ingredients: polenta/coarse cornmeal, the ragu bianco, butter, parmesan
steps: Cook polenta low and whisking in salted water until soft and no longer grainy, 25-30 min.
Beat in a knob of butter and a handful of parmesan until loose and creamy.
Reheat the ragu while the polenta finishes.
Pool the polenta in warm bowls, spoon the ragu over, lots of black pepper and more parm.

dinners.name: White Bean Ribollita
dinners.ingredients: the cannellini conserva + liquor, cavolo nero/kale, onion-carrot-celery, day-old crusty bread, olive oil, parmesan
steps: Build a quick soffritto in olive oil, add shredded cavolo nero and wilt.
Add the beans with all their liquor plus water to cover; simmer 10-15 min.
Tear in day-old bread and stir until it melts into a thick porridge.
Finish with a heavy drizzle of new olive oil and grated parmesan.

technique.name: Mantecatura (pan-emulsifying pasta)
technique.tiedTo: Pappardelle al Ragu Bianco. The payoff of the ragu: pull the pasta early, finish it in the sauce, then off the heat beat in cold butter, parmesan and starchy water and toss hard until it emulsifies into a glossy, clinging sauce rather than a watery one. Aim for silky, not soupy, not greasy.

shopping.items: 2 yellow onions, 2 carrots, 1 bunch celery, 2 heads garlic, fresh sage, fresh rosemary, flat-leaf parsley, 2 bunches cavolo nero/lacinato kale (or escarole), 2 lemons, 1 dried chile
2 cod or halibut fillets (~12 oz total)
1 pint whole milk, parmesan wedge (with rind), butter
1 oz dried porcini, 1 lb dried cannellini beans, dry white wine, pappardelle, polenta/coarse cornmeal, day-old crusty bread, bay leaves, good finishing olive oil

scaleNote: This week is just the two of you (girls with Jen through ~Oct 17), so portions are for 2 and the components are deliberately batched to carry four dinners. When the girls are back (full house of 6): both components already scale, but double the ragu again and cook ~1.5 lb pappardelle; ragu over pasta or soft polenta is an easy kid win. Ribollita scales linearly. For the fish night, flake extra cod over buttered beans or plain pasta for the girls and go light on lemon, and add garlic bread to stretch the table.
